summary: Iteration 235: Verified P0 URN Overwrite Bug Fix via code review and frontend smoke tests. The fix ensures PRO transaction payloads use on-chain profile URN (from API data) instead of user.urn (which can be the Bitcoin address placeholder). Backend health check passed. Frontend loads correctly with login, feed, and settings working.

critical_code_review_comments: MyProfilePage.js (Lines 130-137): FIXED - Uses profile?.urn || profile?.URN from API data, guards against address-as-URN with explicit check: onChainUrn !== activeAddress && onChainUrn !== user?.address
SettingsModal.js (Lines 1088-1093): FIXED - Uses authProfileUrn prop (resolved on-chain URN), guards against address match: resolvedUrn === user?.address
ActivateMessaging.js (Lines 33-50): FIXED - Fetches profile from API, checks both data?.URN and data?.urn (case-mismatch fix), guards against address-as-URN: profileData.urn === user?.address
useAuth.js (Lines 171-172, 245-246): Confirmed - Still sets urn=address as placeholder, which is OK because downstream consumers now properly guard against it

p0_bug_verification.bug_description: Profile updates were overwriting the user's on-chain URN with their Bitcoin address. This happened because useAuth.js sets urn=address as a fallback, and MyProfilePage.js/SettingsModal.js/ActivateMessaging.js blindly submitted this address as the URN in PRO payloads.
p0_bug_verification.fix_verification: Code review confirms all 3 files now use on-chain profile URN from API data (not user.urn) and guard against address-as-URN submission. The fix prevents the bug by: (1) Fetching real URN from profile API, (2) Checking if URN equals address before submission, (3) Showing user-friendly error if no minted profile exists.
p0_bug_verification.test_user_status: Test user 'Emergent2' already has minted profile with active messaging, so guards would allow operation to proceed correctly using on-chain URN.
